I'm making the switch from iPhone to the S26 Ultra, and honestly, it's all about everyday usability. On the iPhone, you can't simply swipe back from the right edge of the screen. And checking notifications or opening Control Center on such a massive phone is unnecessarily frustrating. On Samsung, you can swipe down anywhere on the home screen to access notifications and quick settings without stretching your thumb to the top. Yes, iPhone has Reachability, but it's a clunky workaround that doesn't always work smoothly. Then there's Samsung's proper multitasking, split-screen apps, customization, and actual freedom to use your phone the way you want. And let's talk about the S Pen — absolutely amazing for editing YouTube Shorts and Instagram Reels, especially when working with text, animations, and precise adjustments. Apple makes fantastic hardware, but iOS still feels years behind in basic usability. In 2026, I shouldn't have to fight a €1,000+ phone just to perform simple tasks with one hand. Time for a change! 🔥

Honestly, the iPhones released this year feel like they weren't ready for production, and Apple Support seems completely unprepared to deal with the issues. I paid $1,400 for an iPhone 18 Pro Max, waited a MONTH for delivery, and found display inconsistencies right out of the box. Enabling Display Pulse Smoothing (PWM), lowering brightness, and checking in a dark room made the issue around the Dynamic Island much easier to spot. I tested several other 18 Pro and Pro Max units belonging to friends and coworkers. Some showed the same issue, some didn't, and the defects varied between one side and both sides. My phone has a Samsung G9N panel. Apple Store staff initially mentioned a replacement, made me wait two hours for an appointment, then offered a screen repair instead. Apple Support gave me conflicting answers, with one person saying I'd have to pay for a repair and another saying my only option was to return the phone. I even bought AppleCare+ after a representative assured me it would guarantee a replacement. They couldn't deliver on that, and the next day I was offered a replacement for another $99! I spent HOURS on calls trying to avoid returning the phone and transferring all my data again. The last representative even wanted me to share my screen to demonstrate a physical display issue. One representative said they were receiving an overwhelming number of calls about the same problem. I have recordings of every conversation. I wanted to make a Reddit post with photos to warn other buyers, but Reddit keeps removing it. Absolutely unacceptable for a company like Apple. I guess I'll stick with my iPhone 15 Pro.
